standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used in the induction at the end of the counted proof (lines 36289-36292)

core_obligations: Use that regular local rings are Cohen-Macaulay to identify, in each of the two rings, generation of the kernel by a regular sequence with generation by the expected number of elements (proof lines 36266-36269).

Compare the two ideals along the surjection from the regular local ring onto the intermediate one, and finish by induction on the minimal number of generators, dividing out by a regular element (proof lines 36270-36293).
proof_roadmap: Reduce each pair of conditions to a single counting condition (proof lines 36266-36269).
Transfer the condition along the surjection and induct on the number of generators (proof lines 36270-36294).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for surjective local homomorphisms between regular local rings, four conditions on the kernels (generation by a regular sequence, or by the expected number of elements, on either side) are equivalent (statement lines 36254-36264). The proof does not recompute dimensions: it uses that regular local rings are Cohen-Macaulay so that each pair of conditions collapses to a counting condition, relates the two kernels along the surjection, and finishes by an induction dividing out a regular element, which decreases dimension and generator count together (proof lines 36266-36294). Seeing that the induction preserves the numerical agreement is the content. H2.
